claims.statement: On one master critical lattice, the ideal d-row partial Fourier section has exact depth-heterogeneity excess E_d=8 sum_{n<d}(d-n)|sum_r z_r(n) cosh(a_r n/P)|^2.

Every finite weighted bank of nested row sections collapses to scalar weights W_n multiplying the same depth moment at each master frequency. Proper shorter supports do not create independent cosh(alpha theta a) channels.

One full support plus any finite fixed-ratio proper nested supports cannot yield a first-order interface gap for three arbitrary depth classes: an endpoint-null direction satisfies Q_theta=O(theta^3), hence Q_theta/theta tends to zero.

The preceding M-1 aligned-channel theorem remains mathematically valid only for genuinely independent depth-response channels. Ordinary Zeta23 support ratios 1 and 3/4 do not automatically instantiate those channels in the master-lattice partial-frame model.
